entities.name: Publius Egnatius Celer
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Publius Egnatius Celer was a Stoic philosopher of Roman origin, born into a prominent equestrian family in the 1st century CE. His significance lies in his controversial career as a delator, or informer, during the reign of Nero, which ultimately led to his death in the reign of Vespasian.



 His case highlights the treacherous nature of political loyalty and the dangers of unchecked power.



 As a Stoic, Celer's philosophical views emphasized reason, self-control, and indifference to external events.
